subject: amber snail
title: This Snail's Eyes Pulse Like Caterpillars. They Aren't Its Eyes

scenes.text: This snail's eyes are pulsing. And they are not its eyes anymore.
A flatworm has stuffed both eyestalks with striped sacs that throb 75 times a minute.
To a bird, they look like fat caterpillars. And the worm can only breed inside a bird.
So it drives the snail. Infected snails climb high and sit in full sun. Healthy ones hide.
A bird rips off the stalk and swallows it. The snail lives. The worm grows a new sac.
And the eyes start pulsing again. For the rest of its life.

description:
The amber snail's eyestalks pulse like caterpillars, but what is pulsing is a parasitic flatworm, Leucochloridium paradoxum.
Its broodsacs throb 40 to 75 times a minute, and a 2014 University of Wroclaw study found infected snails climb higher, stay in the light and keep moving, so birds spot them. A bird tears off the stalk, the snail survives, and the worm grows a new sac.
What is the creepiest parasite you know? Comment below.
first_comment: The snail can live a year or more like this, and the worm has no brain, no nerves and no eyes, yet it only pulses in daylight, when birds hunt. Which parasite should we cover next?
